Here's a clean and robust JavaScript solution using regular expressions:

```javascript
function removeAge(text) {
  // 1. Remove "(age X)" where X is any number
  // 2. Collapse multiple spaces into one
  // 3. Trim leading/trailing whitespace
  return text.replace(/\(age\s+\d+\)/gi, '')
             .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
             .trim();
}

// Example usage:
const input = "july 7 1994 (age 7) London, UK (1994-07-07)";
const result = removeAge(input);

console.log(result); 
// Output: "july 7 1994 London, UK (1994-07-07)"
```

### 🔍 How it works:
| Part | Explanation |
|------|-------------|
| `\(age\s+\d+\)` | Matches `(age `, followed by **one or more spaces** (`\s+`), followed by **any number** (`\d+`), followed by `)` |
| `gi` flags | `g` = replace all occurrences, `i` = case-insensitive (handles `(Age 12)`, `(AGE 5)`, etc.) |
| `.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')` | Cleans up double spaces left behind after removal |
| `.trim()` | Removes accidental leading/trailing spaces if `(age X)` was at the start/end |

### ✅ Test Cases:
```javascript
console.log(removeAge("july 7 1994 (age 7) London, UK (1994-07-07)"));
// "july 7 1994 London, UK (1994-07-07)"

console.log(removeAge("Born (age 25) in Paris"));
// "Born in Paris"

console.log(removeAge("(Age 100) New York, USA (2023-01-01)"));
// "New York, USA (2023-01-01)"
```
